Header.Name: Source
Header.Description: Minimum and mandatory metadata elements common to all resources.

Element.name: nameOrTitle
Element.Documentation: The name of a Source. For Sources: Use a user-friendly name to identify the source. Depending on the Source type, this may contain a combination of it's name, year of creation, creator, et cetera.

Element.name: mainType
Element.Documentation: Recommendation for vocabularies to use: https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dcat-3/#Property:resource_type. You can use a term from the PiCo thesaurus for Source types: https://terms.personsincontext.org/sourcetypes . (Internal note: this property is related but is not the same as this one in PiCo: https://schema.org/additionalType).

Element.name: additionalSourceType
Element.Documentation: "An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org style guide." See PiCo's vocabulary: https://personsincontext.org/model/#https://schema.org/additionalType

Element.name: internalType
Element.Documentation: To use for internal classification of sources (e.g., primary, secondary; or any other useful classifications which vary per project).

Element.name: accessURL
Element.Documentation: A URL of the resource that gives access to it. In PiCo: A media object, usually a scan, that encodes the Source of a Person observation (https://schema.org/associatedMedia).

Element.name: landingPage
Element.Documentation: Optional: A Web page that can be navigated to in a Web browser to gain access to the catalog, a dataset, [a source], its distributions and/or additional information (e.g., HTML page with description, metadata, links, DOI landing page, catalog page, Zotero item page)

Element.name: abstract
Element.Documentation: An abstract is a short description that summarizes a CreativeWork.

Element.name: zoteroGroupItemLink
Element.Documentation: Add here the link to the item in the Zotero group: 1) go to https://www.zotero.org/groups/6097405/ecodicesnl. 2) Right-click on the item and select the option "copy link". 3) Paste the link here. Here's an example item URL: https://www.zotero.org/groups/4804340/hereyourgroupname/items/EQ2D34GW

Component.name: Keywords
Component.Documentation: Add as many keywords as wanted, making sure they have URIs.

Component.name: Identifiers
Component.Documentation: Internal note: for Letters (profile v2), the URI should be mapped to: https://lod.academy/cer/vocab/ontology#21_Identifier. CIDOC path: ->P1->E42[1_1]->P190->rdf:Literal.

Element.name: identifierType
Element.Documentation: The type/scheme of identifier (e.g., "Wikidata QID", "VIAF", "project local"

Element.name: identifierValue
Element.Documentation: Add the identifier's label (e.g., the shelfmark, or the identifier number in another scheme). If you chose "Other" in the Identifier type, enter here in parenthesis where the identifier comes from, for example: N011111 (Nodegoat).

Element.name: identifierUri
Element.Documentation: Persistent identifier (optional): If the object has a permanent identifier (e.g., a URN, DOI, or handle), enter the full IRI here (e.g., https://resolver.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de/SBB00019E8400000003). It does not need to be resolvable. If it is OpenStreetMaps: Enter the URI from OpenStreetMap API. You can search directly in OpenStreetMaps and paste the URI here. The URI has to have this format, for example: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/214885 (note the type in the middle: relation, node, way)

Element.name: noteType
Element.Documentation: Add any specific types of notes to the controlled vocabulary.

Component.name: RecordWorkflowStatus
Component.Documentation: Explained in the project documentation (add link:...)

Element.name: recordStatus
Element.Documentation: To indicate the stage the record is at in terms of completeness. For example, for a Source: all relevant data has been extracted from the source, or if there is still data that could be extracted at a later stage. For an Entity observation: if it is an initial draft, or if all the observation-related data is entered.

Element.name: noteType
Element.Documentation: Add any specific types of notes to the controlled vocabulary.
